dedupe_keys.name: euro ix annual ixp reports 2007 to 2021

description: The European Internet Exchange Association (Euro-IX), a non-profit association of internet exchange points founded in Amsterdam in 2001, published yearly reports on the state of internet exchange points in Europe with a global overview, from 2007 to 2021. Each report compiles figures from its members and, in later years, from the IXP database (IXPDB) that Euro-IX runs, which collects data hourly from exchanges' own systems. The 2021 edition, 38 pages, covers the number of connected networks by exchange and by regional association, exchanges compliant with the MANRS routing security actions, traffic growth over ten years among members, global and top-ten traffic statistics, port price distributions over five years for each port speed, and the switching platforms and peering hardware in use in Europe. Earlier reports give long series: the number of operational exchanges in Europe rose from 102 in 2005 to 224 in 2019 and 255 in 2020, and average aggregated peak traffic among members from 955 Gbit/s in 2007 to 18,765 Gbit/s in 2016. Coverage: Europe in detail, with global comparisons, 2005 to 2021. Format and access: PDF reports on the Euro-IX website, free. Caveats: no report after 2021 was found; figures depend on voluntary member returns and definitions changed between editions; tables are in PDF only. Simulation uses: growth and capacity trends of interconnection, costs of exchange ports for economic models, and concentration of traffic at large exchanges for network and failure studies. Related records: the Euro-IX IXP database holds the live data behind later reports, and the PCH directory and PeeringDB list exchanges worldwide.
